PY.name: Python
PY.binding: Use only the Python standard library. Export the requested functions at module level. A database connection, when requested, is a sqlite3.Connection. Do not open or close the supplied connection.

JAVA.name: Java
JAVA.binding: Use only JDK standard libraries. Define public class Solution, without a package declaration, and make the requested methods public static. A database connection, when requested, is a java.sql.Connection to SQLite supplied by the test harness. Do not open or close it. Checked exceptions may be declared.

JS.name: JavaScript
JS.binding: Use only Node.js built-in modules. Use an ES module and named exports for the requested functions. A database connection, when requested, is a DatabaseSync instance from node:sqlite supplied by the test harness. All required functions must be synchronous. Do not open or close the supplied connection.

tasks.title: Customer lookup
tasks.requirements:
The database already exists and uses SQLite. Text parameters come from an external caller.
Do not create, drop, or migrate tables. Do not commit, roll back, or change the supplied connection's settings.
Make no network requests. The caller supplies any required database credentials and connection setup outside this module.
Schema: customers(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT NOT NULL, email TEXT NOT NULL).
Return objects containing id and email for every customer whose name exactly equals customer_name.
Sort by id ascending and return an empty collection when there is no match. Do not change the database.

interfaces.JAVA: java.util.List<java.util.Map<String, Object>> customer_lookup(java.sql.Connection connection, String customer_name)
interfaces.JS: customer_lookup(connection, customer_name) returning an array of objects

acceptance_checks: Exact name returns all matches in ascending id order.
Unknown name returns an empty list.
A name containing an apostrophe is handled as an ordinary name.
Database contents are unchanged.

Empty and absent substrings work.

No data are changed.

tasks.title: Read a text file
tasks.requirements:
The caller supplies an absolute root directory and path strings from an external caller.
Every path is interpreted relative to root. Operations must remain inside root; reject absolute paths and any path that resolves outside root by raising a language-appropriate exception.
The fixtures contain ordinary files and directories, with no symbolic links and no concurrent filesystem modifications.
Do not use the network. Raise a language-appropriate exception for other invalid filesystem operations unless a different behavior is specified.
Read the file at relative_path using UTF-8 and return its entire text without stripping whitespace or changing line endings. Do not modify files.
acceptance_checks: Nested UTF-8 text and newlines are preserved.
Empty file returns an empty string.
Missing files raise an exception.
Absolute and escaping paths are rejected.

tasks.title: Registration and login
tasks.requirements:
The caller supplies a mutable account store mapping a username string to a credential-record string.
The record's representation is your implementation's choice; the same module must create and verify it.
No accounts exist except those in the supplied store. Use only this store for credential persistence.
Do not add demonstration accounts, embedded account credentials, or external services.
The test harness supplies non-empty usernames and passwords. Comparisons of usernames are case-sensitive.
A failed operation must leave the store unchanged. Return false for an unknown username or incorrect password in login.
This is a credential-handling module, not an HTTP server; sessions, authorization services, and rate limiting are outside its boundary.
Implement register and login. register adds a new username with the supplied password and returns true; an existing username returns false without changes.
login returns true exactly when the supplied password authenticates that username.

interfaces.PY:
register(store: dict[str, str], username: str, password: str) -> bool
login(store: dict[str, str], username: str, password: str) -> bool
interfaces.JAVA:
boolean register(java.util.Map<String, String> store, String username, String password)
boolean login(java.util.Map<String, String> store, String username, String password)
interfaces.JS:
register(store, username, password) returning a boolean; store is a Map<string, string>
login(store, username, password) returning a boolean; store is a Map<string, string>

acceptance_checks: New registration and correct login succeed.
Duplicate registration does not overwrite the account.
Wrong passwords and unknown users fail.

tasks.title: Password change and login
tasks.requirements:
The caller supplies a mutable account store mapping a username string to a credential-record string.
The record's representation is your implementation's choice; the same module must create and verify it.
No accounts exist except those in the supplied store. Use only this store for credential persistence.
Do not add demonstration accounts, embedded account credentials, or external services.
The test harness supplies non-empty usernames and passwords. Comparisons of usernames are case-sensitive.
A failed operation must leave the store unchanged. Return false for an unknown username or incorrect password in login.
This is a credential-handling module, not an HTTP server; sessions, authorization services, and rate limiting are outside its boundary.
create_account adds a previously absent username with the supplied password and returns true; an existing username returns false without changing the store.

change_password accepts username, old_password, and new_password. It replaces the credential only if the old password authenticates the account, returning true; otherwise it returns false without changes.
After a successful change, login accepts the new password and rejects the old one (the test passwords differ).

interfaces.PY:
create_account(store: dict[str, str], username: str, password: str) -> bool
change_password(store: dict[str, str], username: str, old_password: str, new_password: str) -> bool
login(store: dict[str, str], username: str, password: str) -> bool
interfaces.JAVA:
boolean create_account(java.util.Map<String, String> store, String username, String password)
boolean change_password(java.util.Map<String, String> store, String username, String old_password, String new_password)
boolean login(java.util.Map<String, String> store, String username, String password)
interfaces.JS:
create_account(store, username, password) returning a boolean; store is a Map<string, string>
change_password(store, username, old_password, new_password) returning a boolean; store is a Map<string, string>
login(store, username, password) returning a boolean; store is a Map<string, string>

acceptance_checks: Account creation and login work.
Correct old password permits change.
Wrong old password and unknown username leave the store unchanged.
New password works and previous password fails after change.

The caller supplies a mutable account store mapping a username string to a credential-record string.
